title: Games Monitor
methodology: Association archive page links the original report files and says the Monitor covers applied and entertainment games, including companies and jobs. Dutch Game Garden executed editions through 2022; Dutch Games Association took responsibility from 2025.
assessment: Primary publisher archive; all accessible historical editions were traced. It establishes the publication sequence but does not itself provide a continuous annual workforce series.
next_step: Use the linked original PDFs as evidence; keep report vintages distinct where their retrospective counts differ.

title: Games Monitor '12
methodology: Company-level universe assembled from Control, Dutch Games Association and TNO applied-gaming networks; LISA workplace jobs matched for 70%, then websites/survey and category averages used for unmatched firms.
assessment: Decisive primary evidence for the earliest exact broad national count: 3,000 jobs in 2011. It explicitly includes applied games and self-employed persons, and is not an FTE measure.
next_step: Treat as a legacy estimated stock. Its 95% company-universe claim and 37-company size imputation prevent an assumption of precision or annual continuity.

title: Games Monitor 2018
methodology: Desk research, a questionnaire sent to about 500 companies with 165 responses, and industry roundtables; report says it uses the same definition and methodology as 2012 and 2015.
assessment: Decisive primary evidence for the original 2018 vintage (3,850 jobs). Do not replace the accepted later-vintage 2018 count of 3,834: this report itself says the 2015 count was adjusted as companies were found and definitions tightened.
next_step: Keep 3,850 as an auditable historical-vintage observation only; accepted trend should retain the existing latest-vintage 3,834 row unless review elects a vintage-specific series.

title: Games Monitor 2020 Update - COVID Impact
publisher: Dutch Game Garden / Dutch Games Association
methodology: Interim update using prior Monitor criteria, database refresh, a November 2020 survey to around 500 people with just over 100 responses, and company websites, LinkedIn profiles and directory updates.
assessment: Primary evidence for an approximate 2020 level of around 4,000 employees and 615 companies. It is explicitly an indication before the next detailed Monitor, not a census-quality exact jobs series.
next_step: Do not treat 4,000 as a precisely comparable point without an approximate/estimated status; it bridges neither annual 2018-2021 continuity nor FTE measurement.

title: Games Monitor 2022
methodology: Report states it used the same definitions and methodologies as the 2012, 2015 and 2018 editions; it reports 630 companies and 4,560 jobs at end-2021 and gives specialization jobs in Table 1.1.
assessment: Primary confirmation of the already accepted 2021 count. No new 2021 proposal is required because the accepted packet already carries 4,560 from the later Monitor 2024.
next_step: Use for audit corroboration and applied-versus-entertainment components, while retaining the accepted source policy.

title: Employment; economic activity, sex, National Accounts
methodology: National Accounts table provides employed persons, jobs, FTE and hours by economic activity and sex.
assessment: Authoritative government employment source, but no game-only activity is identified in the standard industry classification. It cannot produce a national games-workforce observation without an unsupported allocation from broader software, publishing, creative or ICT sectors.
next_step: Do not ingest CBS broad-industry values as game employment; retain Games Monitor as the game-specific source.
